Second is the <term>phase of continuity</term> <gloss>xiangxu xiang</gloss>, which depends on <term>discrimination</term> <gloss>zhi</gloss>. It produces sensations of suffering and joy, causing thoughts to arise in correspondence and without interruption.

Regarding the "depends on discrimination" within the phase of continuity, this clarifies the basis for its arising. It means that depending on the previous discrimination of desirable objects, a sensation of joy arises. For undesirable objects, a sensation of suffering arises. Thoughts arise repeatedly and appear in continuous succession. This explains the continuity of the self. Furthermore, it can give rise to <term>delusions</term> <gloss>kleshas</gloss> and <term>moisten karma</term> <gloss>runye</gloss> <note>a Buddhist metaphor where craving provides the "moisture" necessary for karmic seeds to sprout into new rebirths</note>, leading to and sustaining the cycle of <term>birth and death</term> <gloss>samsara</gloss>. This causes the continuity of other states. As the text below states, it "maintains suffering and joy" and so on. Therefore, the original text says it "produces" through "without interruption."

Third is the <term>phase of grasping</term> <gloss>zhiqu xiang</gloss>. This refers to the previous objects of suffering and joy. Because one does not understand that these objects are empty and non-existent, one develops deep grasping.

<summary>This page explains the psychological transition from simple discrimination to a continuous stream of emotional responses and karmic attachment. It details how the mind's failure to recognize the emptiness of objects leads to the cycle of rebirth through grasping.</summary>
<keywords>Phase of Continuity, Phase of Grasping, Karma, Samsara, Suffering and Joy, Discrimination, Awakening of Faith</keywords>
